message.content: {"40": {"original": "DRM is evil, and I refuse to accept or support any system that restricts sharing", "rephrased": "Digital Rights Management (DRM) systems are fundamentally harmful because they prevent users from sharing content, a practice that should be considered a positive right. Consequently, any technology or legal framework that restricts the non-commercial sharing of digital works must be rejected entirely, as such restrictions violate the core principle that people should be free to distribute what they own.", "summary": "DRM is condemned as evil for restricting user freedom to share content."}, "41": {"original": "The current copyright system is hypocritical because it supports businesses that", "rephrased": "The existing copyright framework is deeply hypocritical because, while it claims to exist to support creative artists, it actually functions to protect corporate businesses that exploit creators. This system has evolved into a mechanism that pays musicians and other artists so little that they are effectively going broke, thereby prioritizing the profits of distributors over the livelihoods of the people who create the work.", "summary": "The current copyright system hypocritically harms artists to benefit businesses."}, "42": {"original": "Proposes making DRM-related activities a crime, while rejecting terms like 'pir", "rephrased": "Anti-circumvention laws that criminalize the creation or sale of tools used to bypass Digital Rights Management (DRM) must be eliminated entirely, as these laws unfairly restrict user access to content. Furthermore, terms like 'piracy' and 'protected' should be rejected as deceptive smears; the former insults people who share content, while the latter masks the reality that the system is designed to restrict freedom rather than protect rights. The solution is to replace the current broken system with one that genuinely supports artists without imposing these oppressive restrictions.", "summary": "Anti-circumvention laws must be eliminated and harmful terms rejected."}, "43": {"original": "Free browsers cannot support web standards requiring DRM, forcing a choice", "rephrased": "The implementation of web standards that require Digital Rights Management (DRM) creates an impossible choice for users: they must either abandon free, open-source browsers to access restricted content or surrender their digital freedoms. Since DRM can only be supported by proprietary, non-free software, adopting these standards means accepting a system that subjugates users, whereas maintaining free browsers requires rejecting access to DRM-protected works entirely.", "summary": "Adopting DRM standards forces a choice between free browsers and user freedom."}}
